Inverse Scaling: When Bigger Isn't Better

paper.arxiv.2306.09479

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2306.09479v2. Contest task-size/design and scaling reversal discussion establish benchmark-construction scope. Adverse contest selection does not imply population prevalence or universal model scaling behavior. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Inverse scaling can reverse into U-shaped scaling, and some tasks show inverted-U trends or multiple reversals through training; the authors cannot predict the scale needed for improvement on a given task.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The Inverse Scaling Prize accepted datasets with at least 300 examples, evaluated submitted GPT-3 scaling patterns on held-out model series, and used classification or sequence-completion loss for winning tasks.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Task labels were checked by contractors on random samples of at least 50 examples; contractors could use the internet, and multipart tasks were sampled by part or grouped parts rather than treating all labels as exhaustively verified.
